title: Segmentation Prioritization Worksheet for QBRs and Renewals
content:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet to standardize how we score and prioritize customer accounts for QBR preparation and renewal outreach. The intent is to produce a single priority score per account that balances business value, operational risk, and renewal signals so CS can allocate human attention efficiently.

How to use (quick):
1) Fill the shaded scoring cells for each account (0-5). Use the definitions below.
2) Apply weights in the header row and compute weighted sum -> Priority Score (0-100).
3) Map Priority Score to action tier and follow the Playbook section for outreach cadence and owners.
4) Attach evidence links (dashboard, tickets, notes) in the linked column.

Scoring scale (0-5):
0 = Not applicable / no signal; 1 = very weak / minimal; 2 = low; 3 = average; 4 = strong; 5 = critical / top decile

Core scoring categories (fill per account):
- ARR / ACV (business value): 0-5 — include committed ARR, expansion potential, contract length.
- ICP fit (product-market fit): 0-5 — is the customer in our primary ICP? (AI-native startups, platform teams, regulated enterprise).
- Deployment mode sensitivity: 0-5 — private/dedicated customers are higher touch (private=5, dedicated=4, hosted=2).
- Region complexity: 0-5 — multi-region or APAC/EU compliance complexity (NA-only=1).
- Adoption momentum: 0-5 — trend in API calls, routes enabled, embeddings usage (growth+ vs flat/decline).
- Reliability & Ops risk: 0-5 — recent SRE incidents, latency SLA misses, production bugs.
- Quality risk (regressions): 0-5 — eval failures, model quality regressions, escape incidents.
- Contract health: 0-5 — renewal window, legal/PO signals, payment history.
- Strategic value / referenceability: 0-5 — potential reference customer, marquee brand, case study value.
- Support load: 0-5 — current ticket volume, open P1s, escalation level.

Suggested default weights (tweak per quarter):
- ARR/ACV: 20
- ICP fit: 10
- Deployment mode: 12
- Region complexity: 6
- Adoption momentum: 14
- Reliability & Ops risk: 12
- Quality risk: 8
- Contract health: 10
- Strategic value: 6
- Support load: 2

Priority score calculation (example):
Priority Score = sum(category_score / 5 * category_weight) rounded to integer -> range ~0-100

Example row (text table):
Account: Cobalt Analytics | ARR: $420k | Created by: Maya T.
- ARR/ACV: 4 | ICP fit: 5 | Deployment: 4 (dedicated) | Region: 2 (NA+EU) | Adoption: 4 | Ops risk: 2 | Quality: 3 | Contract health: 3 | Strategic: 4 | Support: 1
Weighted sum -> ((4/5)*20)+((5/5)*10)+((4/5)*12)+((2/5)*6)+((4/5)*14)+((2/5)*12)+((3/5)*8)+((3/5)*10)+((4/5)*6)+((1/5)*2)= 
=16+10+9.6+2.4+11.2+4.8+4.8+6+4.8+0.4 = 69.0 -> Priority Score 69 -> Tier: 1 (High)

Mapping scores to priority tiers (recommended):
- Tier 1 (High) Priority: Score >= 65 -> action: proactive QBR prep, executive involvement, weekly cadence in 60-day renewal window (if in-window), allocate Solutions Eng + AM sync.
- Tier 2 (Medium): Score 40-64 -> action: standard QBR + renewal playbook, biweekly check-ins, ensure health dashboard; plan canary upsell/expansion.
- Tier 3 (Low): Score < 40 -> action: light-touch quarterly check-in, automated renewal reminders, focus CS time on Tier 1/2 accounts.

Playbook snippets (Tier-based):
Tier 1 (High):
- Owners: CS Lead + Solutions Eng + CSM assigned.
- Pre-QBR tasks (2-4 weeks prior): pull cost & latency breakdown, model versions in use, KV cache hit rate, incidents last 90 days, embedding cost trends.
- QBR agenda: 1) Business outcomes alignment (10m) 2) Usage & economics (15m) 3) Technical deep-dive (20m) 4) Roadmap & next steps (10m) 5) Executive summary & ask (5m).
- Renewal window (<90 days): schedule exec-to-exec, propose renewal options (reserved capacity vs burst), prepare pricing scenarios and savings from batching/quantization.

Tier 2 (Medium):
- Owners: CSM primary; SE on consult basis.
- Pre-QBR: highlight adoption patterns and small tactical wins (caching suggestions).
- Cadence: biweekly AM check-ins, monthly product newsletter.

Tier 3 (Low):
- Owners: CSM pooled; outreach via playbook templates, automated health reports.
- Cadence: quarterly automated digest + opt-in QBR.

Renewal outreach sequence (example for Tier 1 with renewal in 60d):
- 60d: Initial renewal intent email + request for strategic priorities meeting.
- 45d: Technical health packet (latency/cost/usage) + proposed renewal scenarios.
- 30d: Exec summary + proposal; follow up meeting booked.
- 14d: Final negotiation and legal/PO escalation.
- 7d: Close loop and confirm PO.

Email subject line templates (pick & personalize):
- "[Customer] + Redwood: Renewal planning & 90d performance review"
- "Quick: strategy + cost-saving options for your Redwood deployment"
- "Action required: Renewal timeline and proposed reserved capacity plan"

First sentence examples to open an outreach:
- "Hi Amy — I want to align on your priorities for next year and share a few ideas to reduce per-token cost by ~20% based on your current call pattern."
- "Hi team — we saw a 30% increase in embeddings usage last quarter; can we sync on how you want to balance cost vs latency?"

QBR prep checklist (tickbox style lines, for CSM to copy into workspace):
- [ ] Confirm renewal date and contract owner
- [ ] Pull last 90 days usage + cost per route
- [ ] Verify model versions and quantization applied
- [ ] Export error and incident summary (SLO breaches)
- [ ] Collect 3 customer success stories / product wins
- [ ] Draft agenda and send invite 2 weeks prior
- [ ] Attach pricing scenarios and projected savings

Evidence column guidance (what to link):
- Links to Console dashboards: per-route latency, token-cost breakdowns
- Support ticket anchors (SRE/SE ticket ids)
- Pendo/Amplitude adoption dashboards or raw API call CSVs
- Contract documents (PDF or Salesforce opp id)

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Should region complexity weight be higher for customers with GDPR + APAC presence? Suggest A/B test next quarter with weight +4 for region.
- Consider adding a "Competitive displacement" flag (are they evaluating other inference vendors) — quick column yes/no.
- Need standard mapping from Salesforce ARR bands to 0-5 ARR score (Maya to work with RevOps).

Appendix: quick scoring cheat-sheet (examples)
- ARR: <$50k=1, $50-250k=2, $250-500k=3, $500-1M=4, >1M=5
- Adoption: flat/decline=1, slow growth=2, steady growth=3, fast growth=4, viral/expansion=5
- Deployment: hosted=2, dedicated=4, private=5

---
This is a living doc — copy into a per-quarter sheet and tweak weights based on renewal outcomes. If you update the weights or scoring rules, add a short rationale here with date and author so we can compare outcome lift next quarter.
